source_name: Ahrefs Official Guide — Paraphrased Research Notes
title: On-page SEO fundamentals — internal research notes
author: Internal notes based on Ryan Law's Ahrefs guide
raw_content:
Treat useful, accurate content that satisfies search intent as the prerequisite for on-page optimization. Small metadata or formatting changes cannot compensate for a page that does not solve the searcher's problem.

Place the target topic in naturally relevant locations, and use heading levels to make the page structure understandable to readers and search systems. Avoid repeating the keyword when it harms clarity.

Write title tags and meta descriptions for the actual result a searcher will receive. They should distinguish the page, set the right expectation, and make the value of clicking clear.

Use short descriptive URLs, useful internal links, credible external references, and informative image treatment. These elements should help people navigate and verify the content, not merely satisfy a checklist.

Review competing pages to find missing subtopics and evidence, then add only the gaps that improve the answer. Monitor search performance and user experience after publication so optimization becomes an evidence-driven loop.
